title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Landscaping
audience: Landscaping operators, including solo operators, who price garden beds, planting, paving and planned works and need to state scope boundaries clearly.
learningOutcomes: Write a landscaping offer with a clear promised result, a time frame, a stated scope boundary and a fair return-visit term
Identify the friction and risk a landscaping client carries and reduce them
Price a landscaping offer on value and on cost, and check it against the sourced market ranges

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'I will do your garden' is a service. 'I will plant the agreed 100 m² bed to the listed plan within an agreed number of weeks, mulch it, and return once in the first month to replace any plant that fails for reasons within my care' is an offer. The client buys a finished bed, a date and a fix. Set the time frame and the return window from your own project records. Name the boundary: planting and mulch only, or planting plus a structure.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: A clear outcome (the bed or area finished to the approved plan); a time frame (the start and finish weeks); the work the client must do (approve the plan, clear access, and confirm any services in the ground with their own checks); the certainty you provide (a signed plan, a materials schedule and photos at each stage, taken with consent); and the risk you carry (the return visit). Put the scope and its boundary in writing. The boundary matters for registration in Victoria: planting, ponds, outdoor furniture, cubby houses, and driveways and paving are generally not domestic building work when contracted alone, while verandahs, pergolas, decks, retaining structures and fencing generally are (Victorian Building Authority, undated). A quote for planting only must say so. In Western Australia a quote becomes binding once accepted (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026). In Victoria a contract exists whether the agreement was verbal or written (Consumer Affairs Victoria, 9 July 2025).

instruction.heading: Reducing friction and approvals
instruction.body: Make the site visit, plan approval and payment steps simple. Record the access route, the material zone, the water tap and any approvals needed from a body corporate or strata committee. Strata guidance says significant design changes, tree removal or major landscaping may require a general meeting resolution, depending on scope and cost (Clean Group, 9 March 2026), so ask the committee early. Deposits: in Western Australia, a deposit should generally be no more than 10 per cent, with payments following completed stages (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026). That is a WA guideline, not a Victorian or NSW rule.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and claims
instruction.body: Consumer guarantees apply to services and cannot be excluded by contract. In Victoria, a tradesperson guarantees due care and skill, fitness for a specified purpose and completion within a reasonable time where none is set (Consumer Affairs Victoria, 9 July 2025). A plant replacement window is an optional promise, so set it at a cost you can carry. Do not state a measurable result, such as no weeds for a year, unless you can show evidence for it. Check current ACCC guidance before publishing any measurable claim.

instruction.heading: Packages that step up in price
instruction.body: A three-level structure suits landscaping projects. Good: a garden plan only. Better: the plan, plus a planting list and a materials schedule. Best: the plan, the planting list, and supply and planting of a defined bed, with a return visit. Market references are from the Melbourne cost guide: a garden design or plan at $720, $1,800 and $4,500; a new garden bed at $45, $90 and $160 per m²; and a landscaper at $50, $72 and $99 per hour (What's the Damage, verified 1 November 2026). The page does not say whether these include GST, so state the GST status on your own quote. Show one total for each tier (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026). Stepped packages with each higher level adding something visible are one way to present the offer (Jobber Academy, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024).

instruction.heading: Pricing on value
instruction.body: Price from the outcome, the scope boundary and the risk, then check against cost and time. Government guidance says a quote should recover every cost and add a margin (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025). A premium is justified when the client receives a finished, documented result with a clear boundary.

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence, such as 'the bed is planted to the approved list and mulched within the agreed weeks'.
Set a time frame and a return window you have checked against past projects.
State the scope boundary in writing, including whether any structure, retaining edge or fence is excluded.
List what the client must do, such as approving the plan and confirming access, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element: a signed plan, a materials schedule and stage photos, with consent.
Price from value and boundary, then check the rate against cost, time and the sourced ranges.

workedExamples.situation: A client asks for a 100 m² new garden bed with planting. The owner is unsure whether the job needs a registered practitioner, and the client asks whether a retaining edge can be added.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the owner offer, and how should the scope be written?
workedExamples.reasoning: At the Melbourne typical rate of $90 per m², a 100 m² planting bed is an illustrative $9,000 (What's the Damage, verified 1 November 2026). The page does not say what that rate includes, so the figure is a rough check only. Planting alone is generally not domestic building work when contracted alone, so the $10,000 registered-practitioner threshold applies only if the work is domestic building work. A retaining edge changes that: retaining structures, decks and fencing are generally domestic building work, and a retaining wall 1 metre or higher needs a building permit (Victorian Building Authority). The owner quotes the planting bed as one package with its boundary written in, and prices any retaining edge separately, after confirming with the VBA or a registered practitioner which band it falls in.

equipmentAndPpe: Written plan with boundary and exclusions
Stage photo record, taken with consent

commonErrors.error: Quoting a planting job that has a retaining or building element hidden in it
commonErrors.prevention: State the boundary in writing, and price structural elements separately after checking the rules.

commonErrors.error: Making a plant guarantee you cannot afford
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the replacement window to a cost you have set and can carry.

commonErrors.error: Quoting without GST status or a single total
commonErrors.prevention: State one total for each tier and say whether GST is included.

commonErrors.error: Ignoring strata approval for major landscaping
commonErrors.prevention: Ask the committee early when a general meeting resolution may be needed.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. Check state rules before acting.

Victoria (VBA, undated): a registered practitioner is needed when the contract price is over $10,000 and the work is domestic building work. Domestic building insurance is required when the cost is more than $16,000. Retaining walls 1 metre or more in height need a building permit. A building permit is not required for a driveway or for laying paving.

NSW (NSW Government, updated 23 June 2026): a licence is required for structural landscaping work carried out under a residential building contract valued at more than $5,000 in labour and materials, including GST.

Pesticide and herbicide application for landscapers in Victoria is not confirmed, so this lesson does not offer chemical treatment in any package. Watering rules for new plantings are state-based, so check the rule for the state and utility before promising a watering schedule.

qualityStandard: Every landscaping offer is written, states its boundary and exclusions, and says whether GST is included.
Each tier price is built from the operator's own costs and checked against the sourced range.
documentationEvidence: Written offer with the outcome, schedule, boundary, exclusions and return-visit terms
Stage photo record, taken with consent
summary: A good landscaping offer promises a finished result, a stated boundary, a date and a fair return visit.
Scope boundaries decide which rules apply, so write them into every quote.
Higher rates follow from clearer value, not from longer hours.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a landscaping offer does the customer buy?
What should a plant replacement guarantee on a landscaping job be?
options: Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new customers and friends
Something you can deliver and afford
